skill.name: example-skill
skill.description: Provides a reference for creating Claude Code plugin skills, including structure, frontmatter, trigger descriptions, content guidelines, and development best practices.
skill.summary: Learn the core structure and writing patterns for Claude Code plugin skills.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives. Five detections are Markdown fences for directory and YAML examples, while the remaining detection is ordinary guidance about avoiding trigger overlap. No malicious commands, prompt injection, or intent-level security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid overlap with other skills' trigger conditions

content.value_statement: Skill authors need a clear reference for structuring and describing plugin skills. This guide explains required files, optional resources, frontmatter, activation wording, and practical design guidelines.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md file and its role in a plugin skill.
Shows basic and extended directory structures for skill projects.
Documents name, description, version, and license frontmatter fields.
Provides a reusable pattern for writing activation descriptions.
Lists practical guidelines for focused, structured, and testable skill content.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not create or validate files automatically.
It covers basic skill structure, not advanced agent orchestration or plugin deployment.
Optional supporting files are illustrative and are not included with this skill.
Actual activation behavior depends on the host model and the final description.

use_cases.title: Create a First Skill
use_cases.description: Learn the minimum directory, frontmatter, and content needed for a basic plugin skill.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Compare an existing skill against the documented file structure and content guidelines.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Use a shared reference when defining skill triggers, supporting resources, and authoring conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the required structure of a Claude Code plugin skill. Include the minimum files and the purpose of each frontmatter field.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when learning skill authoring for the first time.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Activation Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me draft a skill description for [topic]. Include specific user phrases, relevant keywords, and clear topic boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when defining when a skill should activate.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Skill Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill outline: [outline]. Identify missing structure, unclear activation conditions, and content that needs more actionable guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before expanding an outline into a complete SKILL.md file.

prompt_templates.title: Design Supporting Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a focused file structure for a complex [topic] skill. Explain which references, examples, or scripts are justified and how each supports the skill.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning an advanced skill with optional supporting files.

output_examples.input: What files are required for a basic skill?
output_examples.output: A basic skill needs a skill directory containing SKILL.md. That file defines metadata, activation conditions, and the guidance the model should follow.

output_examples.input: What should a useful skill description include?
output: Specific phrases that users may enter.
Keywords that indicate the skill is relevant.
Topic boundaries that distinguish the skill from related skills.

output_examples.input: How should I organize a complex skill?
output_examples.output: Keep SKILL.md as the main definition. Add focused reference, example, or script directories only when they provide material support for the skill.

best_practices: Keep each skill focused on one clear domain.
Write precise activation descriptions with realistic user phrases and keywords.
Test expected prompts and confirm that related skills have distinct trigger conditions.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad descriptions that make the skill activate for unrelated requests.
Do not add supporting files without a clear role in the skill workflow.
Do not replace actionable instructions with general background information.

faq.question: What is the minimum required file?
faq.answer: Each skill requires a SKILL.md file inside its skill directory.

faq.question: Which frontmatter fields are required?
faq.answer: The name and description fields are required. Version and license fields are optional.

faq.question: How does a skill activate?
faq.answer: The model selects a skill from task context and the activation conditions stated in its description.

faq.question: Can a skill include supporting files?
faq.answer: Yes. Complex skills can include references, examples, documentation, and helper scripts when they serve a clear purpose.

faq.question: How should I write the description?
faq.answer: Include specific user phrases, relevant keywords, and the topic areas that the skill covers.

faq.question: Does this skill create plugin files?
faq.answer: No. It provides a reference for structure and content but does not scaffold or validate a plugin.
